tagline: A lakeside town where everyone suddenly disappeared — and the water kept what they left behind.

now.focus: Making the abandoned town feel like it is waiting
now.next: Fog, lake edge, and spaces that might be memory — not just empty rooms

bible.epigraph: The water keeps what we leave behind.
bible.logline: Stillwater is a large, isolated lakeside town mysteriously abandoned after The Stillwater Incident. Cars remain parked. Stores still hold goods. Some buildings still have power. It feels less like evacuation — and more like everyone suddenly disappeared.
bible.inspiration: Keep the town mysterious. Environmental storytelling, uncertainty, isolation and atmosphere matter more than exposition. Water, fog, memory and isolation are the central recurring themes. The town itself should gradually feel like an entity. The player should never completely understand Stillwater.

chapters.title: Core setting
chapters.lede: Tens of thousands once lived here. Today the town sits almost empty beneath persistent fog and overcast skies. Stillwater was never destroyed — it was emptied.
points: Homes still contain personal belongings
Some buildings inexplicably still have electricity
The silence feels wrong — not evacuated, vanished

chapters.title: Stillwater Lake
chapters.lede: The enormous lake beside the town is central to its history. Generations told stories of voices in the fog, shoreline disappearances, lights beneath the water, and the dead seen near the shore.
chapters.quote: The water keeps what we leave behind.
points: Objects wash ashore decades after vanishing
Old Stillwater was flooded when a dam was built
Buildings and roads still exist beneath the lake

chapters.title: The Alder Institute
chapters.lede: A neurological research facility studying memory, trauma and disease. From material beneath the lake they recovered S-0 — a substance that seemed to interact with neurological activity, then to retain memories.
points: Patients remembered events they never lived
Some recalled places they had never visited
Others remembered the lives of the long dead
Alder named the phenomenon Resonance

chapters.title: The Stillwater Incident — 1998
chapters.lede: Alder attempted to amplify Resonance. Something went catastrophically wrong. At 02:17 AM, communications from Stillwater stopped. When authorities entered, almost the entire population was gone — with no sign of evacuation.
points: The government sealed the town
Official story: industrial contamination
The real cause was never publicly revealed

chapters.title: Present day
chapters.lede: Years later, the protagonist receives a message from someone who disappeared during the Incident — originating from inside Stillwater. They return to investigate. The checkpoints are abandoned. The road is open. Stillwater appears to be waiting.

chapters.title: What Stillwater has become
chapters.lede: Something here can turn memory into reality. The town subtly changes around the player. You should never be certain whether you are in reality, a memory, hallucination, Resonance — or something else.
points: A building may look different when revisited
A room may briefly appear as it did decades ago
Objects appear where they were not
Water exists where it physically shouldn't
Human silhouettes move through the fog
Some places hold fragments of past events

chapters.title: The creatures
chapters.lede: Connected to memory, trauma and Resonance — not simply undead. Some resemble distorted humans; others are physical manifestations of memories, fears or trauma tied to people and places. Every important creature needs a reason to exist.

chapters.title: The central mystery
chapters.lede: First: what happened to Stillwater? Then: what was Alder actually doing? Eventually: why does Stillwater seem to recognize the protagonist?
points: Alder looks responsible — at first
Strange events around the lake predate Alder
Alder did not create what lives here — they discovered it, experimented, and may have awakened it

narrativeRules.title: Narrative rules
narrativeRules.lede: Rules for every scene, enemy and system — use these when deciding what belongs in Stillwater.
points: Keep Stillwater mysterious — do not scientifically explain every supernatural event
Do not turn the story into a simple virus outbreak
Alder is not an obvious cartoon-evil corporation; the research began with legitimate medical aims before becoming unethical
Avoid constant gore and jumpscares
Environmental storytelling, uncertainty, isolation and atmosphere beat exposition
Water, fog, memory and isolation are the recurring themes
The town should gradually feel like an entity
The player should never completely understand Stillwater

priority.label: Atmosphere
priority.note: Fog, emptiness, the sense the town is waiting.

priority.label: Tension
priority.note: Uncertainty — reality vs memory vs Resonance.

priority.label: Exploration
priority.note: Lake edge, Old Stillwater echoes, rooms that change.

priority.label: Survival
priority.note: Scarcity and safe rooms against an entity-like place.

priority.label: Spectacle
priority.note: Earn revelations. Never lead with gore or cheap shocks.
